idiom_name: amqplib channel.nack(msg, false, false) / channel.reject -> RabbitMQ dead letter exchange
implementation_notes: In AMQP 0-9-1 the invalid channel is broker topology rather than application code: a queue declared with a dead-letter exchange (preferably through a policy, not x-arguments) republishes any message the consumer rejects with basic.reject or basic.nack and requeue=false. amqplib exposes exactly that as channel.nack(message, allUpTo, requeue) and channel.reject(message, requeue), so the client's whole job is the decision to reject without requeue; the broker adds x-death and x-first-death-* annotations that tell the error handler why and from where the message came.
pitfalls: Nacking with requeue=true puts the message straight back at the head of the same queue and turns one bad message into an infinite loop.
If the dead-letter exchange is missing when the message is dead-lettered, RabbitMQ drops it silently - declare the exchange and binding before the queue or the invalid channel is a black hole.
Dead-lettering is publishing: it runs without publisher confirms by default, and channel-level errors invalidate the whole amqplib channel, so the error path can itself lose the frame.
